_meta.name: Curated Clinical Formulary
_meta.scope: Hackathon MVP. Common self-limiting primary-care presentations only.
_meta.disclaimer: This formulary grounds AI DRAFT generation only. It is never authorization to prescribe. Every entry requires doctor review before reaching a patient.
_meta.review_status: Curated for demonstration. NOT clinically validated for real patient use.

protocols.presentation: Fever with generalized body ache, chills, malaise and headache. No localizing or red-flag features.

medications.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
medications.instructions: Take with water after food. Do not exceed 4,000 mg in 24 hours.

protocols.instructions: Maintain oral hydration with water and ORS. Avoid heavy physical exertion. Seek doctor care if fever exceeds 102 F, persists beyond 4 days, or new symptoms appear.
escalate_if: fever in an infant under 3 months

protocols.presentation: Runny nose, sneezing, mild sore throat and non-productive cough without fever or respiratory distress.

medications.name: Cetirizine Hydrochloride
medications.instructions: May cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery after taking.

medications.name: Warm Saline Gargle and Steam Inhalation
medications.instructions: Inhale warm steam for 5-10 minutes and gargle with warm salt water.

protocols.instructions: Drink warm liquids and rest. Monitor for breathing difficulty, chest tightness or high fever.

protocols.condition: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease without oesophagitis / Dyspepsia
protocols.presentation: Burning retrosternal or epigastric discomfort, sour eructation, worse after meals or lying flat.

medications.name: Pantoprazole
medications.instructions: Take 30 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach with plain water.

medications.name: Antacid Oral Gel (Magaldrate with Simethicone)
medications.instructions: Shake well before use. Take 1-2 teaspoons when experiencing acid burn.

protocols.instructions: Avoid spicy, oily and fried food. Eat small frequent meals. Do not lie down for 2 hours after eating. Elevate the head of the bed.
escalate_if: chest pain radiating to arm or jaw

protocols.presentation: Bilateral, band-like, pressing head pain of mild to moderate intensity without neurological deficit.

medications.name: Paracetamol
medications.instructions: Take after light food with water. Maintain hydration.

protocols.instructions: Ensure adequate rest and hydration of 2-3 litres per day. Reduce screen exposure and take regular breaks.
escalate_if: headache with fever and neck stiffness
headache with weakness or slurred speech

protocols.presentation: Loose stools without blood, without high fever and without signs of significant dehydration.

medications.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
medications.instructions: Dissolve one sachet completely in 1 litre of clean drinking water. Drink after every loose motion.

medications.name: Probiotic Spores (Bacillus clausii)
medications.instructions: Drink directly or dilute in a small amount of water.

protocols.instructions: Eat a light bland diet such as banana, rice and yoghurt. Avoid milk, greasy and fried food. Watch for signs of dehydration.

protocols.presentation: Recurrent sneezing, itchy watery eyes and clear nasal discharge, often seasonal or exposure related.

medications.name: Levocetirizine
medications.instructions: Take at night. May cause mild drowsiness.

protocols.instructions: Identify and avoid the trigger where possible. Use a mask in dusty environments. Rinse nasal passages with saline.

protocols.presentation: Burning or painful urination with urinary frequency and urgency, in a non-pregnant adult with no fever or flank pain.

medications.name: Nitrofurantoin
medications.instructions: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Complete the full course even if symptoms improve early.

protocols.instructions: Drink plenty of water. Avoid holding urine for long periods. Complete the full antibiotic course.

protocols.presentation: Red eye with sticky yellow-green discharge and crusting, eyes stuck together on waking, without pain or vision change.

medications.name: Chloramphenicol Eye Drops (0.5%)
medications.instructions: Wash hands before use. Wipe away discharge with clean water before instilling. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye.

protocols.instructions: Avoid sharing towels or pillows. Wash hands frequently to prevent spread. Discontinue contact lens use until resolved.

protocols.presentation: Itchy ring-shaped rash with a clear centre and raised scaly border, or peeling skin between the toes.

medications.name: Clotrimazole Cream (1%)
medications.instructions: Apply to the affected area and 2 cm beyond the visible edge. Continue for a week after the rash clears to prevent recurrence.

protocols.instructions: Keep the area clean and dry. Avoid sharing towels or clothing. Wear breathable footwear if the feet are affected.

protocols.presentation: Throbbing, pulsating headache typically one-sided, with light sensitivity and nausea, sometimes preceded by an aura.
keywords: pulsating pain on one side of head

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.frequency: As needed, up to three times daily
medications.instructions: Take at the earliest sign of an attack with food. Do not exceed 3 doses in 24 hours.

medications.name: Domperidone
medications.instructions: Take 15-30 minutes before the pain reliever if nausea is prominent.

protocols.instructions: Rest in a dark, quiet room. Identify and avoid personal triggers (skipped meals, poor sleep, certain foods). Keep a headache diary if attacks are frequent.
escalate_if: attacks increasing in frequency or severity

protocols.presentation: Upper abdominal fullness and early satiety after meals, without the meal-timed retrosternal burning typical of reflux.

medications.name: Domperidone
medications.instructions: Take 15-30 minutes before eating.

protocols.instructions: Eat smaller, more frequent meals. Avoid lying down immediately after eating. Reduce caffeine and carbonated drinks.

protocols.presentation: Itchy, fluid-filled blisters in crops spreading over the body, often with mild fever.

medications.name: Calamine Lotion
medications.instructions: Apply to itchy lesions with a clean cotton pad. Keep nails short to reduce scratching and scarring.

medications.name: Chlorpheniramine
medications.instructions: May cause drowsiness. For itching relief, particularly at night.

protocols.instructions: Isolate from pregnant women, newborns and immunocompromised individuals until all lesions have crusted. Keep the patient hydrated and cool.
escalate_if: lesions become painful and spreading red (secondary bacterial infection)

protocols.presentation: Intense itching, worse at night, classically involving the finger webs, wrists and groin, often with similar symptoms in household contacts.

medications.name: Permethrin Cream (5%)
medications.duration: Apply once, wash off after 8-14 hours; repeat after 7 days
medications.instructions: Apply to the entire body from neck down, including under nails and between fingers. All household contacts should be treated simultaneously.

protocols.instructions: Wash all bedding, clothing and towels in hot water. Treat all household and close contacts at the same time to prevent reinfestation.

protocols.presentation: White, curd-like patches on the tongue or inner cheeks, sometimes with mild soreness, that can be wiped off leaving a red base.

medications.name: Nystatin Oral Suspension
medications.instructions: Swish around the mouth for as long as possible before swallowing. Continue for 2 days after symptoms clear.

protocols.instructions: Rinse mouth after meals. Denture wearers should clean and soak dentures overnight. Consider checking blood sugar if recurrent.

protocols.presentation: Honey-coloured crusted sores, often around the nose and mouth, sometimes with oozing, most common in children.

medications.name: Mupirocin Ointment (2%)
medications.instructions: Gently clean crusts with soap and water before application. Cover with a light dressing to prevent spread.

protocols.instructions: Keep the child home from school/daycare until 24 hours of treatment is complete. Avoid sharing towels. Wash hands frequently to prevent spread.
escalate_if: extensive involvement beyond a small area

protocols.presentation: Ear pain worsened by pulling the ear or jaw movement, itchy ear canal, sometimes with discharge, often after water exposure.

medications.name: Ciprofloxacin + Dexamethasone Ear Drops
medications.instructions: Lie with the affected ear up for 2-3 minutes after instilling. Keep the ear dry during treatment.

protocols.instructions: Keep the ear dry; avoid swimming until resolved. Do not insert cotton buds into the ear canal.

protocols.presentation: Severe throat pain with fever, visible white patches or pus on the tonsils, and painful swallowing, distinct from a routine viral sore throat.
keywords: difficulty swallowing with fever and swollen glands

medications.name: Amoxicillin
medications.instructions: Take with or without food. Complete the full course even if symptoms improve within a few days.

protocols.instructions: Warm salt-water gargles for comfort. Maintain hydration and soft diet. Rest voice if hoarse.
escalate_if: symptoms worsening after 3 days of antibiotics

protocols.presentation: Facial pain or pressure over the cheeks and forehead, worse on bending forward, with nasal congestion, typically following a cold.

medications.name: Pseudoephedrine
medications.instructions: Avoid taking in the evening as it can cause insomnia. Do not exceed 5 days of continuous use.

medications.name: Saline Nasal Irrigation
medications.instructions: Use isotonic saline rinse to clear nasal passages.

protocols.instructions: Steam inhalation may provide symptomatic relief. Most acute sinusitis is viral; antibiotics are reserved for symptoms persisting beyond 10 days or worsening after initial improvement.

protocols.presentation: Persistent cough, often productive of mucus, continuing after the other cold symptoms have resolved, without breathlessness or chest pain.
keywords: productive cough with mucus after cold

medications.name: Dextromethorphan Cough Syrup
medications.instructions: Take for troublesome dry cough. Not for use in a productive/wet cough where suppressing clearance is undesirable.

protocols.instructions: Steam inhalation and warm fluids may ease symptoms. Antibiotics are not indicated for uncomplicated viral bronchitis. Avoid smoke exposure.

protocols.presentation: Crampy lower abdominal pain occurring with menstrual periods, without abnormal bleeding or pain outside the menstrual cycle.
keywords: pet me dard periods ke dauran

medications.name: Mefenamic Acid
medications.duration: During painful days of the cycle, up to 5 days
medications.instructions: Take with food. Start at the onset of pain or bleeding for best effect.

protocols.instructions: A heating pad on the lower abdomen may help. Regular light exercise can reduce symptom severity over time.
escalate_if: pain not responding to standard analgesia

protocols.presentation: Infrequent, hard stools with straining, without alarm features such as bleeding or weight loss.

medications.name: Isabgol (Psyllium Husk)
medications.instructions: Mix in a full glass of water or milk and drink immediately. Ensure adequate fluid intake throughout the day.

medications.name: Lactulose
medications.instructions: May take 1-2 days to take effect. May cause bloating initially.

protocols.instructions: Increase dietary fibre, fluids and physical activity. Establish a regular toileting routine.
escalate_if: no bowel movement for over a week
new constipation in an older adult

protocols.presentation: Discomfort or bleeding with bowel movements, itching or a lump near the anus, without severe pain or dark blood.

medications.name: Hydrocortisone + Lidocaine Cream
medications.instructions: Apply to the affected area after gentle cleaning. Do not use for more than 7 days continuously.

protocols.instructions: Increase dietary fibre and fluids to soften stool. Avoid straining. Warm sitz baths may relieve discomfort.
escalate_if: a hard, very painful lump (possible thrombosis)

protocols.presentation: Facial or truncal pimples, blackheads and whiteheads on oily skin, without deep painful nodules or scarring.

medications.name: Benzoyl Peroxide Gel (2.5%)
medications.frequency: Once daily, increasing to twice daily as tolerated
medications.instructions: Apply to clean, dry skin. Start with once daily to build tolerance; may cause dryness or peeling initially. Use sunscreen during the day.

protocols.instructions: Wash affected areas gently twice daily; avoid harsh scrubbing. Avoid picking or squeezing lesions. Results take 6-8 weeks; do not switch products too soon.
escalate_if: sudden severe flare with systemic symptoms

protocols.presentation: Itchy, red patches at the site of contact with a trigger substance, or dry itchy patches in a typical eczema distribution.

medications.name: Hydrocortisone Cream (1%)
medications.instructions: Apply only to affected areas. Avoid use on the face for more than 5 days without review.

medications.name: Emollient (Fragrance-Free Moisturiser)
medications.instructions: Apply generously, especially after bathing.

protocols.instructions: Identify and avoid the triggering substance (jewellery, detergent, cosmetic). Use fragrance-free skin products.
escalate_if: signs of infection (increasing redness, warmth, pus)

protocols.presentation: Itchy, raised, migratory welts that appear and resolve within hours, without breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

medications.name: Levocetirizine
medications.instructions: Take at bedtime; may cause mild drowsiness.

protocols.instructions: Identify and avoid a possible trigger (new food, medication, contact). Cool compresses may soothe itching.
escalate_if: swelling of lips, tongue or throat

protocols.presentation: Nausea, dizziness and queasiness occurring during travel by car, boat or air, resolving once travel stops.

medications.name: Dimenhydrinate
medications.instructions: Take 30-60 minutes before travel. Causes drowsiness; avoid driving.

protocols.instructions: Sit facing forward and fix gaze on the horizon. Avoid reading during travel. Keep well ventilated.
escalate_if: associated with headache or neurological symptoms

protocols.presentation: Brief spinning sensation triggered specifically by head movement or position change (rolling over, looking up), without hearing loss or other neurological signs.

medications.name: Betahistine
medications.instructions: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.

protocols.instructions: Move slowly when changing position. Sit on the edge of the bed for a moment before standing.
escalate_if: hearing loss or ringing in the ear
vertigo lasting continuously beyond a day

protocols.presentation: Localised pain and mild swelling after exercise, lifting or a twisting injury, with the joint or limb still usable.

medications.name: Diclofenac Gel (1%)
medications.instructions: Massage gently into the affected area. Wash hands after application.

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.instructions: Take with food.

protocols.instructions: Rest, ice, compression and elevation (RICE) for the first 48 hours. Gradually resume activity as tolerated.
escalate_if: unable to bear weight or use the limb at all

protocols.presentation: Dull, aching lower back pain, often after lifting or prolonged sitting, without radiation below the knee, numbness or bladder/bowel symptoms.

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.instructions: Take with food.

medications.name: Diclofenac Gel (1%)
medications.instructions: Apply to the lower back and massage gently.

protocols.instructions: Stay active within pain limits; prolonged bed rest delays recovery. Use correct lifting technique and posture.
escalate_if: pain radiating down the leg below the knee
numbness in the groin or inner thighs
loss of bladder or bowel control

protocols.presentation: Gritty, dry or tired feeling in the eyes, often after prolonged screen use, without discharge, pain or vision change.

medications.name: Carboxymethylcellulose Lubricant Eye Drops
medications.frequency: As needed, up to four times daily
medications.instructions: Preservative-free formulation preferred with frequent use. Remove contact lenses before instilling.

protocols.instructions: Follow the 20-20-20 rule during screen use (every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds). Blink deliberately and ensure adequate room humidity.
escalate_if: sensation of a foreign body not relieved by drops

protocols.presentation: Itchy, mildly swollen area at the site of a mosquito or insect bite, without spreading redness, fever or systemic symptoms.

medications.name: Calamine Lotion
medications.instructions: Apply directly to the bite site.

medications.name: Cetirizine
medications.instructions: Take at bedtime if itching is significant; may cause drowsiness.

protocols.instructions: Avoid scratching to reduce infection risk. A cold compress can reduce swelling.
escalate_if: swelling of lips, tongue or throat

protocols.presentation: Vaginal itching with thick, white, non-malodorous discharge, without fever or pelvic pain.

medications.name: Clotrimazole Vaginal Pessary (500 mg)
medications.instructions: Insert high into the vagina at bedtime. May use an accompanying external cream for vulval itching.

protocols.instructions: Wear breathable cotton underwear. Avoid douching and scented feminine products.
escalate_if: recurrent infections (4 or more per year)

protocols.presentation: Localised tooth or jaw pain, often worse with hot, cold or sweet stimuli. This protocol provides temporary symptomatic relief only and does not treat the underlying dental cause.

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.instructions: Take with food. This is temporary relief only — a dentist must assess the cause.

medications.name: Clove Oil (Topical)
medications.dosage: A few drops on a cotton pledget
medications.instructions: Apply directly to the affected tooth for temporary numbing.
cautions: avoid contact with gums for extended periods

protocols.instructions: This is temporary symptomatic relief only. A dentist must assess and treat the underlying cause — a prescription here is not a substitute for a dental visit.
escalate_if: difficulty opening the mouth or swallowing
pain not controlled by standard analgesia

protocols.presentation: Itchy scalp with visible lice or nits (eggs) attached to hair shafts, common in school-age children.

medications.name: Permethrin Lotion (1%)
medications.duration: Leave on for 10 minutes, then rinse; repeat after 7 days
medications.instructions: Apply to dry hair and scalp, leave for the specified time, then rinse and comb with a fine-tooth comb. Treat all affected household members simultaneously.

protocols.instructions: Wash bedding, combs and hats in hot water. Check and treat all household contacts. Repeat treatment after 7 days to catch newly hatched lice.
escalate_if: signs of secondary skin infection (spreading redness, pus)
treatment failure after two full courses
